parsedContent.method: 1) Contour plowing: Align plow lines along the natural contour of the slope. Erosion risk is estimated by E = (R * S) / (C * V) where R is rainfall intensity, S is slope length, C is soil cohesion and V is vegetation cover; the formula divides by the product of cohesion and cover, weighting the effect of each. 2) Terracing: Build a series of level steps on steep slopes. The terrace stability factor T = (L * B) / (W * D) where L is terrace length, B is bench width, W is wall height and D is drainage coefficient; division by wall height and drainage coefficient weights structural support and water removal. 3) Cover crops: Plant a protective vegetative layer. The protective index P = (C * R) / (E) where C is crop density, R is root depth and E is exposed soil area; division by exposed area weights the reduction in soil exposure.
keyPoints: Contour plowing aligns tillage with slope contours to slow runoff and reduce shear stress.
Terracing creates flat benches that break slope length, dissipating energy and providing physical barriers to erosion.
Cover crops increase ground cover and root networks, protecting soil from raindrop impact and increasing infiltration.
